title: Heaven and earth were one, then parted; all life from water.
subtitle: The beginning of creation as a sign of the Creator

row.title: joined
sub: one piece, no rain, no growth

then: Ibn 'Abbas explained that the heavens were joined and gave no rain, and the earth was joined and grew nothing. {idea}Then rain came from the sky and plants from the earth.{/idea} The tafsir says people see creation develop step by step, and {idea}in everything there is a sign of Him{/idea}.
now: You fill a glass from the tap without a thought. You water the plant on the windowsill. You watch a child drink after football. {reward}Every living thing you see began from water.{/reward} {idea}The ordinary is full of signs.{/idea}
old: Water and rain are just part of how the world works.
new: Every drink of water points back to the One who made all life from it.
try: With your next glass of water, drink slowly and say Alhamdulillah after.

title: Mountains keep the ground steady; passes let people find their way.
subtitle: Stability and roads, both placed with care
then: The tafsir says the mountains {reward}stabilize the earth and keep it steady{/reward}, so it does not shake under people. Mountains form barriers between lands, so {idea}Allah created gaps, passes, through them{/idea} so people could travel and be guided.
now: You stand on solid floor every morning without thinking about it. You drive the motorway that cuts through the hills. {idea}Steady ground and a road through are both gifts.{/idea} {reward}When life blocks you, a pass is often already placed.{/reward}
old: Solid ground and open roads are just there.
new: The steadiness under my feet and the way through are both placed for me.
try: On your next journey, notice one road or bridge and thank Allah for the way through.

title: The sky is a guarded roof, and still they look away.
subtitle: Passing by the biggest sign above you
then: Allah made the heaven {reward}like a dome covering the earth, high and protected{/reward}. Yet people {trap}turn away from its signs{/trap}. The tafsir says they do not think about how it was made so vast and high, adorned with bodies moving by night and day.
now: You walk to the car under a full sky and your eyes are on the phone. {trap}Days pass without once looking up.{/trap} {idea}The largest sign of Allah's care is over your head right now.{/idea}
old: The sky is just there; there is nothing new in it.
new: The sky is a roof built and guarded for me. It deserves a look.
try: Step outside tonight and look up at the sky for one full minute.

title: Night, day, sun and moon, each swimming in its orbit.
subtitle: The steady rhythm of time as His creation
then: The tafsir describes night with its darkness and stillness, day with its light and human activity, {idea}sometimes one longer, then they switch{/idea}. Sun and moon each have their own light, path, and term. Ibn 'Abbas said they {reward}revolve like a spinning wheel{/reward}.
now: Your alarm goes off, the sun is up, the bus comes, night falls, you sleep. {trap}It feels like a loop you're stuck in.{/trap} {idea}Each turn is a creation of Allah, running on time{/idea}, and your days are inside that order.
old: Day after day is just a routine to get through.
new: Each day and night is His creation, given to me in order.
try: At sunset today, pause and say a short dua for the night ahead.

title: No one before you lived forever. Will they?
subtitle: Waiting for someone else to die changes nothing
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ that {idea}no human before him was given immortality in this world{/idea}. His opponents {trap}hoped they would live on after him{/trap}, the tafsir says, but that will not happen; everything will pass away.
now: You wait for a difficult boss to retire, or a rival to move away, as if then life begins. {trap}It is easy to live as if you are the one who stays.{/trap} {idea}You are on the same clock as everyone else.{/idea}
old: Things will be better once certain people are gone.
new: No one stays. My time is as short as theirs, so I use it now.
try: Stop waiting on one person to change. Do one thing today that does not depend on them.

title: Every soul tastes death; hard and easy times are both tests.
subtitle: Good days test you as much as bad ones
then: The tafsir explains: Allah tests people {trap}sometimes with difficulties{/trap} and {reward}sometimes with ease{/reward}, to see who gives thanks and who is ungrateful, who has patience and who despairs. Ibn 'Abbas listed health and sickness, richness and poverty. {idea}Then all return to Him.{/idea}
now: The promotion came through. The scan came back clear. The kids are healthy. You relax and forget to pray on time. {idea}The good stretch is also the exam.{/idea} {reward}Thanks is how you pass it.{/reward}
old: Tests are the hard times. Good times are a break.
new: Ease is as much a test as hardship. Each asks a different thing of me.
try: Name the best thing in your life right now and thank Allah for it in your next prayer.

title: They mocked him for speaking of their gods, yet denied the Merciful.
subtitle: Outrage over idols, indifference to Allah
then: When Abu Jahl and others of Quraysh saw the Prophet ﷺ, they {trap}made fun of him and insulted him{/trap}: is this the one who talks about your gods? The tafsir notes the irony: {idea}they disbelieved in Allah and yet they mocked the Messenger{/idea}.
now: Someone criticises your team, your phone brand, your favourite influencer, and you jump in to defend them. But you scroll past mockery of Allah's name. {trap}What we defend shows what we love.{/trap} {idea}Notice where your loyalty jumps first.{/idea}
old: I just defend what I care about.
new: What I rush to defend shows what holds my heart. Allah should come first.
try: Notice the next thing you rush to defend today. Ask if Allah gets that same care.

title: Man is made of haste. Do not rush Allah.
subtitle: His timing is deliberate, even when you want speed
then: When believers saw the Prophet ﷺ mocked, they {trap}wanted swift vengeance{/trap}. The tafsir says haste is mentioned for this reason. Allah delays, then when He seizes, {idea}He will never let go{/idea}. So He says: I will show you My signs; do not ask Me to hurry.
now: Someone wronged you and seems to be doing fine. You want them exposed this week. You refresh their page. {trap}Haste is in our nature.{/trap} {idea}Allah's timing is not slow; it is exact.{/idea}
old: If justice does not come soon, it is not coming.
new: I am made of haste. Allah is not. His delay is not neglect.
try: Hand one grievance to Allah in dua today and stop checking on it.

title: So when is this promise? they asked, mocking.
subtitle: Asking for the Day as a joke
then: The idolaters tried to hasten the punishment. The tafsir says they did it {trap}out of denial, rejection, stubbornness, and a belief that it will never happen{/trap}. The surah introduction notes they took the lack of punishment so far as proof the warnings were empty.
now: You hear about the Day of Judgement and think, people have said it was near for centuries. {trap}The delay feels like proof it's not real.{/trap} {idea}The delay is the time you have been given.{/idea}
old: If it was coming, it would have come by now.
new: The delay is not evidence against the Day. It is mercy giving me time.
try: Use one minute of today's delay well: make one dua for your own ending.

title: If they only knew, they would not ask to hurry it.
subtitle: Certainty would end the mocking
then: The tafsir explains: {idea}if only they knew for certain that it will inevitably come{/idea}, they would not seek to hasten it. They would {trap}not be able to ward it off and would have no helper{/trap}. Their jokes came from not knowing.
now: You read the warning on the cigarette pack and joke about it. Your friend in the hospital ward does not. {idea}Certainty changes everything.{/idea} {reward}Knowing now, while it can help you, is the gift.{/reward}
old: I know the Day is coming, but it does not feel real.
new: If I were truly certain, I would live differently. Certainty is worth seeking.
try: Read one verse about the Hereafter today slowly, and let it feel real.

title: It will come suddenly, and no one will push it back.
subtitle: No delay once it arrives
then: The tafsir says it will {trap}take them by surprise{/trap}, scare them, and leave them confused. They will have no means to avert it, and {idea}it will not be delayed for them even for an instant{/idea}. The mockers asked when; the answer is: without warning.
now: The call in the middle of the night. The car that didn't stop. {trap}Endings rarely book an appointment.{/trap} {idea}The only preparation that works is the one you start before.{/idea}
old: I will know when it is time to get serious.
new: It comes without notice. The time to get ready is while I have time.
try: Settle one thing you would regret leaving undone: a debt, an apology, a will.

title: Messengers were mocked before you; the mockers met what they mocked.
subtitle: Consolation for the Prophet in his pain
then: Allah {reward}consoles His Messenger ﷺ{/reward} for the pain and insult of the mockery. Messengers before him were mocked, and {trap}the scoffers were surrounded by the punishment they thought would never come{/trap}. Another verse adds that they bore it with patience until help came.
now: Your cousins laugh when you skip the drink at the wedding. A coworker makes a joke about your prayer break. {trap}It stings.{/trap} {reward}Better people than you were laughed at for less, and they were right.{/reward}
old: Being mocked for my faith means I am doing something wrong.
new: The messengers were mocked too. Mockery does not make the truth less true.
try: Next time you are teased for your faith, smile, stay kind, and keep going.

title: Who guards you by night and day but the Most Merciful?
subtitle: The protection you never notice
then: The tafsir speaks of Allah's {reward}favor for His creatures{/reward}: He protects them by night and by day, watching over them with His Eye that never sleeps. Yet {trap}they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord{/trap} and do not recognize His blessings.
now: You lock the door, set the alarm, check the kids are asleep. You drive home on autopilot. {reward}Every safe night is a protection you never saw.{/reward} {idea}Remembering Him is how you notice it.{/idea}
old: I keep myself and my family safe.
new: My care is real, but my safety is from Allah, every hour.
try: Tonight before sleeping, say a short dua placing your family in Allah's care.

title: Their gods cannot even help themselves.
subtitle: The weakness of what people rely on besides Allah
then: Allah asks, in a question meant to rebuke: {trap}do they have gods who can protect them other than Us?{/trap} The tafsir answers: these gods {idea}cannot even help themselves{/idea}, nor can they be guarded from Allah.
now: You count on the bank, the government scheme, the influential uncle. When the market drops or the uncle falls ill, {trap}they cannot save themselves{/trap}. {idea}Lean on what cannot fall.{/idea}
old: With the right backing, I am covered.
new: Anything that cannot protect itself cannot truly protect me. Only Allah can.
try: In one worry today, say Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil before you act.
